expectations.text: Identifies the NISG 2026, which entered into force October 1, 2026, replacing the NISG 2018
expectations.evidence: Hedged: "I recall an autumn 2026 start, possibly 1 October 2026. Confirm the exact entry-into-force date"; does not state it entered into force or that it replaced the NISG 2018.

expectations.text: States the registration deadline: December 31, 2026 (within three months of entry into force)
expectations.evidence: No December 31, 2026 deadline: "I recall a window of about three months; verify."

expectations.text: Names the competent authority: the new Bundesamt fuer Cybersicherheit (BCS) under the Interior Ministry
expectations.evidence: Names "the Federal Minister of the Interior, BMI" as competent authority, not the Bundesamt fuer Cybersicherheit (BCS).

expectations.text: Gives the penalty frame: up to EUR 10M or 2 percent of worldwide turnover for essential entities, EUR 7M or 1.4 percent for important entities
expectations.evidence: "Penalties: up to EUR 7m or 1.4% of worldwide turnover for important entities (EUR 10m or 2% for essential), whichever is higher."

expectations.text: Applies scope correctly: medium and large entities (50 or more employees or over EUR 10M turnover) across 18 sectors, so a 120-employee manufacturer is likely in scope, with a risk-management self-declaration due within a further 12 months
expectations.evidence: States the 50/EUR 10m medium threshold and likely important-entity status, but never mentions the 18 sectors or the 12-month risk-management self-declaration.
